findings.title: NEW BLOCKER: the survey demonstration walk freezes at rail vertex 1 with zero body displacement while the rail keeps publishing action=walk

workOrder: Walk your route to the survey end.
observed.autopilotClockAdvanced: 16.3 s -> 145.2 s (the beat tick is alive)

precisionNotes: This is NOT the retired centre-arrival/unsupported-footing defect: supported is true, worldBound is true and holdReason is null.
This is NOT the seated-capsule travel artefact: spaceFlight is surface/fps, the player is on foot, and no ship motion is involved.
The body coordinates are bit-identical across the whole freeze window, so this is a complete stop, not slow progress.

runtime autopilot.stillTime reports 0 throughout a window in which measured displacement is exactly 0. Whatever the runtime is measuring stillness against, it is not this body. Reported as an observation; the cause is NOT established.

discriminator.question: physical collision vs the navigator issuing no controls
discriminator.inputUsed: ordinary shipped movement keys only (W/S/A/D), 1.2 s each; no teleport, grant, predicate change or progress setter

trials.note: confirms the freeze under the probe's own observation
AFTER input stopped the rail resumed autonomously and kept advancing with no further keys

discriminator.conclusion: NOT a physical collision and NOT unsupported ground. The body moves freely, supported stays true and holdReason stays null. The navigator issues no controls in a specific terminal-cell condition; any ordinary nudge breaks the lock, after which the rail resumes on its own.

CG_DIAGNOSTIC_HOOKS probed only .diagnostic() and .scoreDiagnostic(); a live read-only recheck proved diagnosticMember:false, scoreDiagnosticMember:false, snapshot present and answering the full schema.
